question: Ashish bought some rulers at the rate of ₹180/dozen. He sold them for ₹24 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of 1 ruler = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

Ratio of CP : SP = 15 : 24 = 5 : 8

Profit is 3 parts on a base CP of 5 parts.

Profit % = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of 1 dozen (12) rulers = ₹180

Selling price of 1 ruler = ₹24

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 Profit Calculation
 
 CP = ₹15
 
 Profit = ₹9
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Selling Price (SP) = ₹24
 

 Profit % = 60%
 Result: Profit % = (9 ÷ 15) × 100 = 60%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost price of 1 ruler (CP) = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

⇒ Profit earned on 1 ruler = 24 − 15 = ₹9

⇒ Profit % = (9 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Selling Price is less than Cost Price, Loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, equivalent discount = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)%.
